messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

                    - generic:
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e163]: "Atalanta 41 (3/4): 335-347, Wiirzburg (2010), ISSN 0171-0079"
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e164]: A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by
                        - generic [ref=e165]: V. I. KUZNETZOv from Vietnam and deposited in the
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e166]: Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg
                        - generic [ref=e167]: by
                        - generic [ref=e168]: SVETLANA V. NEDOSHIVINA
                        - generic [ref=e169]: received 4.XTI.2009
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e170]: "Abstract: 67 species described by V. KuzNerzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descrip-"
                        - generic [ref=e171]: tions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7-9). Descriptions of 99 of five species are provided and their
                        - generic [ref=e172]: genitalia are figured.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e173]: "Zusammenfassung: 67 Arten die von V. Kuznetzov aus Vietnam beschrieben wurden, werden mit kurzen Kommentaren zur Ty-"
                        - generic [ref=e174]: pusserie und deren Etikettierung versehen. Die Holotypen werden farbig abgebildet (col. pl. 7-9). Von fünf Arten werden die 99
                        - generic [ref=e175]: beschrieben und deren Genitalien abgebildet.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e176]: "Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists."
                        - generic [ref=e177]: He was born 28.11.1929 in Kingisepp, Leningrad Region. His father was née Egorov and he was born into the family of a smith.
                        - generic [ref=e178]: Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name
                        - generic [ref=e179]: KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage
                        - generic [ref=e180]: until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the
                        - generic [ref=e181]: biological faculty of Leningrad State University in 1946. He finished there in 1951 and completed his PhD in 1954. In 1955 Kuz-
                        - generic [ref=e182]: NETZOV became a staff member at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Leningrad, Russia (ZISP) where
                        - generic [ref=e183]: he worked for 52 years. He took part in several expeditions and published more than 200 papers devoted to Lepidoptera, especially
                        - generic [ref=e184]: Tortricidae. Most of his works dealt with the Palaearctic fauna, but some of them were based on material from the Oriental Regi-
                        - generic [ref=e185]: on. In total, KuzNEtzov described 394 taxa, 295 of them Tortricidae. He died 22. VIII 2008 in St. Petersburg and was cremated at
                        - generic [ref=e186]: Smolenskoe Cemetery.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e187]: Twice in his lifetime, in 1986 and 1988, KuzNetzov visited Vietnam as a member of Soviet-Vietnamese zoological expeditions.
                        - generic [ref=e188]: "The first field trip was carried out in spring and all material was collected in the Northern provinces: Son La, Vinh Phuc and Thai"
                        - generic [ref=e189]: Nguyen (earlier Bac Thai). The second trip was in autumn (9.X1.-22.XII.) and during this time KuzNetzov visited the south of the
                        - generic [ref=e190]: country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov
                        - generic [ref=e191]: in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13
                        - generic [ref=e192]: papers devoted to Tortricidae of Vietnam but only one of them was in English. In these works he listed 225 species, described 67 of
                        - generic [ref=e193]: them as new, and established 5 new genera.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e194]: Investigation of the type material is an important part of all taxonomic studies but detailed descriptions of the species, with figured
                        - generic [ref=e195]: genitalia of both sexes and coloured images of the moths, make the work much easier. Descriptions of Tortricidae from Vietnam
                        - generic [ref=e196]: published by Kuznetzov in 1988-2003 are quite full and figures of genitalia structures are very good. Unfortunately, he gave no
                        - generic [ref=e197]: photos of the type specimens and all his descriptions were published in Russian. So the work with KUZNETzov’s papers is very com-
                        - generic [ref=e198]: plicated without knowledge of the Russian language.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e199]: In recent years the volume of newly collected material from South-East Asia has really increased; a lot of new species are described
                        - generic [ref=e200]: recently from this region. At the same time, coloured images are very important for the comparison of new material with the species
                        - generic [ref=e201]: already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them
                        - generic [ref=e202]: are placed now in the same genera as in the original description. Very few of them were synonymized and mentioned by other workers
                        - generic [ref=e203]: at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that
                        - generic [ref=e204]: some species were described by Kuznetzov based on a single specimen, in most cases g, and 99 are unknown.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e205]: All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by KuZNETZov were arranged taxonomically within the main collection of ZISP. Each speci-
                        - generic [ref=e206]: men has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality (in English). Most of them have a label with the name of the
                        - generic [ref=e207]: species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text “Ho-
                        - generic [ref=e208]: lotypus” or “Paratypus” and the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. KuzNETzov never made genitalia slides
                        - generic [ref=e209]: and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels.
                        - generic [ref=e210]: Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of
                        - generic [ref=e211]: Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where KuzNetzov deposited all material he currently worked on. Some of those
                        - generic [ref=e212]: Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten
                        - generic [ref=e213]: labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few
                        - generic [ref=e214]: of them were marked with red type labels. So specimens belong to the type series were discovered by comparison of their labels with
                        - generic [ref=e215]: the original descriptions. Names of localities mentioned on KuzNEtzov’s labels often differ from modern names and in some cases it
                        - generic [ref=e216]: is difficult to find them on the map. Therefore the list of collecting localities by Kuznetzov is given below with notes on real names
                        - generic [ref=e217]: and coordinates of corresponding places.
                        - generic [ref=e218]: 1. Prov. Sonla, Naniu - According to the map published by Kuznerzov in 2000, this locality is situated between 22° 07° and 22°
                        - generic [ref=e219]: 11° N, 102° 59° and 103° 09° E. Probably this point on the map was identified by KuzNetzov inexactly and actually corres-
                        - generic [ref=e220]: ponds to Ban Nam Nhié situated at 22° 08‘ N, 102° 45‘ E.
                        - generic [ref=e221]: 2. Prov. Sonla, Chiengkhouan or Chienghouan - Province Son La, Ban Chiéng Khoang, 21° 33° N, 103° 40° E.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

                        - generic [ref=e176]: "Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists."

                        - generic [ref=e178]: Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name
                        - generic [ref=e179]: KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage
                        - generic [ref=e180]: until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the

                        - generic [ref=e190]: country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov
                        - generic [ref=e191]: in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13

                        - generic [ref=e198]: plicated without knowledge of the Russian language.

                        - generic [ref=e201]: already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them

                        - generic [ref=e203]: at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that

                        - generic [ref=e209]: and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels.
                        - generic [ref=e210]: Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of

                        - generic [ref=e212]: Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten
                        - generic [ref=e213]: labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e176]: "Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists."
                        - generic [ref=e177]: He was born 28.11.1929 in Kingisepp, Leningrad Region. His father was née Egorov and he was born into the family of a smith.
                        - generic [ref=e178]: Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name
                        - generic [ref=e179]: KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage
                        - generic [ref=e180]: until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the
                        - generic [ref=e181]: biological faculty of Leningrad State University in 1946. He finished there in 1951 and completed his PhD in 1954. In 1955 Kuz-
                        - generic [ref=e182]: NETZOV became a staff member at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Leningrad, Russia (ZISP) where
                        - generic [ref=e183]: he worked for 52 years. He took part in several expeditions and published more than 200 papers devoted to Lepidoptera, especially
                        - generic [ref=e184]: Tortricidae. Most of his works dealt with the Palaearctic fauna, but some of them were based on material from the Oriental Regi-
                        - generic [ref=e185]: on. In total, KuzNEtzov described 394 taxa, 295 of them Tortricidae. He died 22. VIII 2008 in St. Petersburg and was cremated at
                        - generic [ref=e186]: Smolenskoe Cemetery.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e187]: Twice in his lifetime, in 1986 and 1988, KuzNetzov visited Vietnam as a member of Soviet-Vietnamese zoological expeditions.
                        - generic [ref=e188]: "The first field trip was carried out in spring and all material was collected in the Northern provinces: Son La, Vinh Phuc and Thai"
                        - generic [ref=e189]: Nguyen (earlier Bac Thai). The second trip was in autumn (9.X1.-22.XII.) and during this time KuzNetzov visited the south of the
                        - generic [ref=e190]: country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov
                        - generic [ref=e191]: in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13
                        - generic [ref=e192]: papers devoted to Tortricidae of Vietnam but only one of them was in English. In these works he listed 225 species, described 67 of
                        - generic [ref=e193]: them as new, and established 5 new genera.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e194]: Investigation of the type material is an important part of all taxonomic studies but detailed descriptions of the species, with figured
                        - generic [ref=e195]: genitalia of both sexes and coloured images of the moths, make the work much easier. Descriptions of Tortricidae from Vietnam
                        - generic [ref=e196]: published by Kuznetzov in 1988-2003 are quite full and figures of genitalia structures are very good. Unfortunately, he gave no
                        - generic [ref=e197]: photos of the type specimens and all his descriptions were published in Russian. So the work with KUZNETzov’s papers is very com-
                        - generic [ref=e198]: plicated without knowledge of the Russian language.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e199]: In recent years the volume of newly collected material from South-East Asia has really increased; a lot of new species are described
                        - generic [ref=e200]: recently from this region. At the same time, coloured images are very important for the comparison of new material with the species
                        - generic [ref=e201]: already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them
                        - generic [ref=e202]: are placed now in the same genera as in the original description. Very few of them were synonymized and mentioned by other workers
                        - generic [ref=e203]: at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that
                        - generic [ref=e204]: some species were described by Kuznetzov based on a single specimen, in most cases g, and 99 are unknown.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e205]: All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by KuZNETZov were arranged taxonomically within the main collection of ZISP. Each speci-
                        - generic [ref=e206]: men has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality (in English). Most of them have a label with the name of the
                        - generic [ref=e207]: species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text “Ho-
                        - generic [ref=e208]: lotypus” or “Paratypus” and the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. KuzNETzov never made genitalia slides
                        - generic [ref=e209]: and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels.
                        - generic [ref=e210]: Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of
                        - generic [ref=e211]: Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where KuzNetzov deposited all material he currently worked on. Some of those
                        - generic [ref=e212]: Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten
                        - generic [ref=e213]: labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few
                        - generic [ref=e214]: of them were marked with red type labels. So specimens belong to the type series were discovered by comparison of their labels with
                        - generic [ref=e215]: the original descriptions. Names of localities mentioned on KuzNEtzov’s labels often differ from modern names and in some cases it
                        - generic [ref=e216]: is difficult to find them on the map. Therefore the list of collecting localities by Kuznetzov is given below with notes on real names
                        - generic [ref=e217]: and coordinates of corresponding places.

                        - generic [ref=e219]: 11° N, 102° 59° and 103° 09° E. Probably this point on the map was identified by KuzNetzov inexactly and actually corres-

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e164]: A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by
                        - generic [ref=e165]: V. I. KUZNETZOv from Vietnam and deposited in the
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e166]: Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg
                        - generic [ref=e167]: by
                        - generic [ref=e168]: SVETLANA V. NEDOSHIVINA
                        - generic [ref=e169]: received 4.XTI.2009
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e170]: "Abstract: 67 species described by V. KuzNerzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descrip-"
                        - generic [ref=e171]: tions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7-9). Descriptions of 99 of five species are provided and their
                        - generic [ref=e172]: genitalia are figured.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e173]: "Zusammenfassung: 67 Arten die von V. Kuznetzov aus Vietnam beschrieben wurden, werden mit kurzen Kommentaren zur Ty-"
                        - generic [ref=e174]: pusserie und deren Etikettierung versehen. Die Holotypen werden farbig abgebildet (col. pl. 7-9). Von fünf Arten werden die 99
                        - generic [ref=e175]: beschrieben und deren Genitalien abgebildet.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e176]: "Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists."
                        - generic [ref=e177]: He was born 28.11.1929 in Kingisepp, Leningrad Region. His father was née Egorov and he was born into the family of a smith.
                        - generic [ref=e178]: Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name
                        - generic [ref=e179]: KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage
                        - generic [ref=e180]: until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the
                        - generic [ref=e181]: biological faculty of Leningrad State University in 1946. He finished there in 1951 and completed his PhD in 1954. In 1955 Kuz-
                        - generic [ref=e182]: NETZOV became a staff member at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Leningrad, Russia (ZISP) where
                        - generic [ref=e183]: he worked for 52 years. He took part in several expeditions and published more than 200 papers devoted to Lepidoptera, especially
                        - generic [ref=e184]: Tortricidae. Most of his works dealt with the Palaearctic fauna, but some of them were based on material from the Oriental Regi-
                        - generic [ref=e185]: on. In total, KuzNEtzov described 394 taxa, 295 of them Tortricidae. He died 22. VIII 2008 in St. Petersburg and was cremated at
                        - generic [ref=e186]: Smolenskoe Cemetery.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e187]: Twice in his lifetime, in 1986 and 1988, KuzNetzov visited Vietnam as a member of Soviet-Vietnamese zoological expeditions.
                        - generic [ref=e188]: "The first field trip was carried out in spring and all material was collected in the Northern provinces: Son La, Vinh Phuc and Thai"
                        - generic [ref=e189]: Nguyen (earlier Bac Thai). The second trip was in autumn (9.X1.-22.XII.) and during this time KuzNetzov visited the south of the
                        - generic [ref=e190]: country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov
                        - generic [ref=e191]: in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13
                        - generic [ref=e192]: papers devoted to Tortricidae of Vietnam but only one of them was in English. In these works he listed 225 species, described 67 of
                        - generic [ref=e193]: them as new, and established 5 new genera.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e194]: Investigation of the type material is an important part of all taxonomic studies but detailed descriptions of the species, with figured
                        - generic [ref=e195]: genitalia of both sexes and coloured images of the moths, make the work much easier. Descriptions of Tortricidae from Vietnam
                        - generic [ref=e196]: published by Kuznetzov in 1988-2003 are quite full and figures of genitalia structures are very good. Unfortunately, he gave no
                        - generic [ref=e197]: photos of the type specimens and all his descriptions were published in Russian. So the work with KUZNETzov’s papers is very com-
                        - generic [ref=e198]: plicated without knowledge of the Russian language.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e199]: In recent years the volume of newly collected material from South-East Asia has really increased; a lot of new species are described
                        - generic [ref=e200]: recently from this region. At the same time, coloured images are very important for the comparison of new material with the species
                        - generic [ref=e201]: already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them
                        - generic [ref=e202]: are placed now in the same genera as in the original description. Very few of them were synonymized and mentioned by other workers
                        - generic [ref=e203]: at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that
                        - generic [ref=e204]: some species were described by Kuznetzov based on a single specimen, in most cases g, and 99 are unknown.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e205]: All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by KuZNETZov were arranged taxonomically within the main collection of ZISP. Each speci-
                        - generic [ref=e206]: men has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality (in English). Most of them have a label with the name of the
                        - generic [ref=e207]: species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text “Ho-
                        - generic [ref=e208]: lotypus” or “Paratypus” and the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. KuzNETzov never made genitalia slides
                        - generic [ref=e209]: and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels.
                        - generic [ref=e210]: Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of
                        - generic [ref=e211]: Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where KuzNetzov deposited all material he currently worked on. Some of those
                        - generic [ref=e212]: Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten
                        - generic [ref=e213]: labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few
                        - generic [ref=e214]: of them were marked with red type labels. So specimens belong to the type series were discovered by comparison of their labels with
                        - generic [ref=e215]: the original descriptions. Names of localities mentioned on KuzNEtzov’s labels often differ from modern names and in some cases it
                        - generic [ref=e216]: is difficult to find them on the map. Therefore the list of collecting localities by Kuznetzov is given below with notes on real names
                        - generic [ref=e217]: and coordinates of corresponding places.
                        - generic [ref=e218]: 1. Prov. Sonla, Naniu - According to the map published by Kuznerzov in 2000, this locality is situated between 22° 07° and 22°
                        - generic [ref=e219]: 11° N, 102° 59° and 103° 09° E. Probably this point on the map was identified by KuzNetzov inexactly and actually corres-
                        - generic [ref=e220]: ponds to Ban Nam Nhié situated at 22° 08‘ N, 102° 45‘ E.
                        - generic [ref=e221]: 2. Prov. Sonla, Chiengkhouan or Chienghouan - Province Son La, Ban Chiéng Khoang, 21° 33° N, 103° 40° E.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

## Navigation policy

## Page size management (critical)

- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.

- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

                        - generic [ref=e164]: A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by
                        - generic [ref=e165]: V. I. KUZNETZOv from Vietnam and deposited in the
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e166]: Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg

                        - generic [ref=e169]: received 4.XTI.2009
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e170]: "Abstract: 67 species described by V. KuzNerzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descrip-"
                        - generic [ref=e171]: tions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7-9). Descriptions of 99 of five species are provided and their
                        - generic [ref=e172]: genitalia are figured.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e173]: "Zusammenfassung: 67 Arten die von V. Kuznetzov aus Vietnam beschrieben wurden, werden mit kurzen Kommentaren zur Ty-"
                        - generic [ref=e174]: pusserie und deren Etikettierung versehen. Die Holotypen werden farbig abgebildet (col. pl. 7-9). Von fünf Arten werden die 99
                        - generic [ref=e175]: beschrieben und deren Genitalien abgebildet.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e176]: "Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists."
                        - generic [ref=e177]: He was born 28.11.1929 in Kingisepp, Leningrad Region. His father was née Egorov and he was born into the family of a smith.
                        - generic [ref=e178]: Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name
                        - generic [ref=e179]: KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage
                        - generic [ref=e180]: until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the
                        - generic [ref=e181]: biological faculty of Leningrad State University in 1946. He finished there in 1951 and completed his PhD in 1954. In 1955 Kuz-
                        - generic [ref=e182]: NETZOV became a staff member at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Leningrad, Russia (ZISP) where
                        - generic [ref=e183]: he worked for 52 years. He took part in several expeditions and published more than 200 papers devoted to Lepidoptera, especially
                        - generic [ref=e184]: Tortricidae. Most of his works dealt with the Palaearctic fauna, but some of them were based on material from the Oriental Regi-
                        - generic [ref=e185]: on. In total, KuzNEtzov described 394 taxa, 295 of them Tortricidae. He died 22. VIII 2008 in St. Petersburg and was cremated at
                        - generic [ref=e186]: Smolenskoe Cemetery.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e187]: Twice in his lifetime, in 1986 and 1988, KuzNetzov visited Vietnam as a member of Soviet-Vietnamese zoological expeditions.
                        - generic [ref=e188]: "The first field trip was carried out in spring and all material was collected in the Northern provinces: Son La, Vinh Phuc and Thai"
                        - generic [ref=e189]: Nguyen (earlier Bac Thai). The second trip was in autumn (9.X1.-22.XII.) and during this time KuzNetzov visited the south of the
                        - generic [ref=e190]: country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov
                        - generic [ref=e191]: in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13
                        - generic [ref=e192]: papers devoted to Tortricidae of Vietnam but only one of them was in English. In these works he listed 225 species, described 67 of
                        - generic [ref=e193]: them as new, and established 5 new genera.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e194]: Investigation of the type material is an important part of all taxonomic studies but detailed descriptions of the species, with figured
                        - generic [ref=e195]: genitalia of both sexes and coloured images of the moths, make the work much easier. Descriptions of Tortricidae from Vietnam
                        - generic [ref=e196]: published by Kuznetzov in 1988-2003 are quite full and figures of genitalia structures are very good. Unfortunately, he gave no
                        - generic [ref=e197]: photos of the type specimens and all his descriptions were published in Russian. So the work with KUZNETzov’s papers is very com-
                        - generic [ref=e198]: plicated without knowledge of the Russian language.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e199]: In recent years the volume of newly collected material from South-East Asia has really increased; a lot of new species are described
                        - generic [ref=e200]: recently from this region. At the same time, coloured images are very important for the comparison of new material with the species
                        - generic [ref=e201]: already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them
                        - generic [ref=e202]: are placed now in the same genera as in the original description. Very few of them were synonymized and mentioned by other workers
                        - generic [ref=e203]: at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that
                        - generic [ref=e204]: some species were described by Kuznetzov based on a single specimen, in most cases g, and 99 are unknown.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e205]: All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by KuZNETZov were arranged taxonomically within the main collection of ZISP. Each speci-
                        - generic [ref=e206]: men has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality (in English). Most of them have a label with the name of the
                        - generic [ref=e207]: species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text “Ho-
                        - generic [ref=e208]: lotypus” or “Paratypus” and the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. KuzNETzov never made genitalia slides
                        - generic [ref=e209]: and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels.
                        - generic [ref=e210]: Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of
                        - generic [ref=e211]: Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where KuzNetzov deposited all material he currently worked on. Some of those
                        - generic [ref=e212]: Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten
                        - generic [ref=e213]: labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few
                        - generic [ref=e214]: of them were marked with red type labels. So specimens belong to the type series were discovered by comparison of their labels with
                        - generic [ref=e215]: the original descriptions. Names of localities mentioned on KuzNEtzov’s labels often differ from modern names and in some cases it
                        - generic [ref=e216]: is difficult to find them on the map. Therefore the list of collecting localities by Kuznetzov is given below with notes on real names
                        - generic [ref=e217]: and coordinates of corresponding places.
                        - generic [ref=e218]: 1. Prov. Sonla, Naniu - According to the map published by Kuznerzov in 2000, this locality is situated between 22° 07° and 22°
                        - generic [ref=e219]: 11° N, 102° 59° and 103° 09° E. Probably this point on the map was identified by KuzNetzov inexactly and actually corres-
                        - generic [ref=e220]: ponds to Ban Nam Nhié situated at 22° 08‘ N, 102° 45‘ E.
                        - generic [ref=e221]: 2. Prov. Sonla, Chiengkhouan or Chienghouan - Province Son La, Ban Chiéng Khoang, 21° 33° N, 103° 40° E.

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

                        - generic [ref=e164]: A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by
                        - generic [ref=e165]: V. I. KUZNETZOv from Vietnam and deposited in the
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e166]: Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg
