                        - generic [ref=e169]: received 4.XTI.2009
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e170]: "Abstract: 67 species described by V. KuzNerzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descrip-"
                        - generic [ref=e171]: tions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7-9). Descriptions of 99 of five species are provided and their
                        - generic [ref=e172]: genitalia are figured.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e173]: "Zusammenfassung: 67 Arten die von V. Kuznetzov aus Vietnam beschrieben wurden, werden mit kurzen Kommentaren zur Ty-"
                        - generic [ref=e174]: pusserie und deren Etikettierung versehen. Die Holotypen werden farbig abgebildet (col. pl. 7-9). Von fünf Arten werden die 99
                        - generic [ref=e175]: beschrieben und deren Genitalien abgebildet.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e176]: "Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists."
                        - generic [ref=e177]: He was born 28.11.1929 in Kingisepp, Leningrad Region. His father was née Egorov and he was born into the family of a smith.
                        - generic [ref=e178]: Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name
                        - generic [ref=e179]: KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage
                        - generic [ref=e180]: until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the
                        - generic [ref=e181]: biological faculty of Leningrad State University in 1946. He finished there in 1951 and completed his PhD in 1954. In 1955 Kuz-
                        - generic [ref=e182]: NETZOV became a staff member at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Leningrad, Russia (ZISP) where
                        - generic [ref=e183]: he worked for 52 years. He took part in several expeditions and published more than 200 papers devoted to Lepidoptera, especially
                        - generic [ref=e184]: Tortricidae. Most of his works dealt with the Palaearctic fauna, but some of them were based on material from the Oriental Regi-
                        - generic [ref=e185]: on. In total, KuzNEtzov described 394 taxa, 295 of them Tortricidae. He died 22. VIII 2008 in St. Petersburg and was cremated at
                        - generic [ref=e186]: Smolenskoe Cemetery.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e187]: Twice in his lifetime, in 1986 and 1988, KuzNetzov visited Vietnam as a member of Soviet-Vietnamese zoological expeditions.
                        - generic [ref=e188]: "The first field trip was carried out in spring and all material was collected in the Northern provinces: Son La, Vinh Phuc and Thai"
                        - generic [ref=e189]: Nguyen (earlier Bac Thai). The second trip was in autumn (9.X1.-22.XII.) and during this time KuzNetzov visited the south of the
                        - generic [ref=e190]: country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov
                        - generic [ref=e191]: in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13
                        - generic [ref=e192]: papers devoted to Tortricidae of Vietnam but only one of them was in English. In these works he listed 225 species, described 67 of
                        - generic [ref=e193]: them as new, and established 5 new genera.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e194]: Investigation of the type material is an important part of all taxonomic studies but detailed descriptions of the species, with figured
                        - generic [ref=e195]: genitalia of both sexes and coloured images of the moths, make the work much easier. Descriptions of Tortricidae from Vietnam
                        - generic [ref=e196]: published by Kuznetzov in 1988-2003 are quite full and figures of genitalia structures are very good. Unfortunately, he gave no
                        - generic [ref=e197]: photos of the type specimens and all his descriptions were published in Russian. So the work with KUZNETzov’s papers is very com-
                        - generic [ref=e198]: plicated without knowledge of the Russian language.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e199]: In recent years the volume of newly collected material from South-East Asia has really increased; a lot of new species are described
                        - generic [ref=e200]: recently from this region. At the same time, coloured images are very important for the comparison of new material with the species
                        - generic [ref=e201]: already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them
                        - generic [ref=e202]: are placed now in the same genera as in the original description. Very few of them were synonymized and mentioned by other workers
                        - generic [ref=e203]: at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that
                        - generic [ref=e204]: some species were described by Kuznetzov based on a single specimen, in most cases g, and 99 are unknown.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e205]: All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by KuZNETZov were arranged taxonomically within the main collection of ZISP. Each speci-
                        - generic [ref=e206]: men has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality (in English). Most of them have a label with the name of the
                        - generic [ref=e207]: species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text “Ho-
                        - generic [ref=e208]: lotypus” or “Paratypus” and the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. KuzNETzov never made genitalia slides
                        - generic [ref=e209]: and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels.
                        - generic [ref=e210]: Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of
                        - generic [ref=e211]: Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where KuzNetzov deposited all material he currently worked on. Some of those
                        - generic [ref=e212]: Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten
                        - generic [ref=e213]: labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few
                        - generic [ref=e214]: of them were marked with red type labels. So specimens belong to the type series were discovered by comparison of their labels with
                        - generic [ref=e215]: the original descriptions. Names of localities mentioned on KuzNEtzov’s labels often differ from modern names and in some cases it
                        - generic [ref=e216]: is difficult to find them on the map. Therefore the list of collecting localities by Kuznetzov is given below with notes on real names
                        - generic [ref=e217]: and coordinates of corresponding places.
                        - generic [ref=e218]: 1. Prov. Sonla, Naniu - According to the map published by Kuznerzov in 2000, this locality is situated between 22° 07° and 22°
                        - generic [ref=e219]: 11° N, 102° 59° and 103° 09° E. Probably this point on the map was identified by KuzNetzov inexactly and actually corres-
                        - generic [ref=e220]: ponds to Ban Nam Nhié situated at 22° 08‘ N, 102° 45‘ E.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

                        - generic [ref=e164]: A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by

                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e170]: "Abstract: 67 species described by V. KuzNerzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descrip-"
                        - generic [ref=e171]: tions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7-9). Descriptions of 99 of five species are provided and their

                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e173]: "Zusammenfassung: 67 Arten die von V. Kuznetzov aus Vietnam beschrieben wurden, werden mit kurzen Kommentaren zur Ty-"
                        - generic [ref=e174]: pusserie und deren Etikettierung versehen. Die Holotypen werden farbig abgebildet (col. pl. 7-9). Von fünf Arten werden die 99
                        - generic [ref=e175]: beschrieben und deren Genitalien abgebildet.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e176]: "Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists."
                        - generic [ref=e177]: He was born 28.11.1929 in Kingisepp, Leningrad Region. His father was née Egorov and he was born into the family of a smith.
                        - generic [ref=e178]: Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name
                        - generic [ref=e179]: KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage
                        - generic [ref=e180]: until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the
                        - generic [ref=e181]: biological faculty of Leningrad State University in 1946. He finished there in 1951 and completed his PhD in 1954. In 1955 Kuz-
                        - generic [ref=e182]: NETZOV became a staff member at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Leningrad, Russia (ZISP) where
                        - generic [ref=e183]: he worked for 52 years. He took part in several expeditions and published more than 200 papers devoted to Lepidoptera, especially
                        - generic [ref=e184]: Tortricidae. Most of his works dealt with the Palaearctic fauna, but some of them were based on material from the Oriental Regi-
                        - generic [ref=e185]: on. In total, KuzNEtzov described 394 taxa, 295 of them Tortricidae. He died 22. VIII 2008 in St. Petersburg and was cremated at
                        - generic [ref=e186]: Smolenskoe Cemetery.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e187]: Twice in his lifetime, in 1986 and 1988, KuzNetzov visited Vietnam as a member of Soviet-Vietnamese zoological expeditions.
                        - generic [ref=e188]: "The first field trip was carried out in spring and all material was collected in the Northern provinces: Son La, Vinh Phuc and Thai"
                        - generic [ref=e189]: Nguyen (earlier Bac Thai). The second trip was in autumn (9.X1.-22.XII.) and during this time KuzNetzov visited the south of the
                        - generic [ref=e190]: country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov
                        - generic [ref=e191]: in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13
                        - generic [ref=e192]: papers devoted to Tortricidae of Vietnam but only one of them was in English. In these works he listed 225 species, described 67 of
                        - generic [ref=e193]: them as new, and established 5 new genera.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e194]: Investigation of the type material is an important part of all taxonomic studies but detailed descriptions of the species, with figured
                        - generic [ref=e195]: genitalia of both sexes and coloured images of the moths, make the work much easier. Descriptions of Tortricidae from Vietnam
                        - generic [ref=e196]: published by Kuznetzov in 1988-2003 are quite full and figures of genitalia structures are very good. Unfortunately, he gave no
                        - generic [ref=e197]: photos of the type specimens and all his descriptions were published in Russian. So the work with KUZNETzov’s papers is very com-
                        - generic [ref=e198]: plicated without knowledge of the Russian language.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e199]: In recent years the volume of newly collected material from South-East Asia has really increased; a lot of new species are described
                        - generic [ref=e200]: recently from this region. At the same time, coloured images are very important for the comparison of new material with the species
                        - generic [ref=e201]: already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them
                        - generic [ref=e202]: are placed now in the same genera as in the original description. Very few of them were synonymized and mentioned by other workers
                        - generic [ref=e203]: at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that
                        - generic [ref=e204]: some species were described by Kuznetzov based on a single specimen, in most cases g, and 99 are unknown.
                      - paragraph:
                        - generic [ref=e205]: All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by KuZNETZov were arranged taxonomically within the main collection of ZISP. Each speci-
                        - generic [ref=e206]: men has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality (in English). Most of them have a label with the name of the
                        - generic [ref=e207]: species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text “Ho-
                        - generic [ref=e208]: lotypus” or “Paratypus” and the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. KuzNETzov never made genitalia slides
                        - generic [ref=e209]: and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels.
                        - generic [ref=e210]: Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of
                        - generic [ref=e211]: Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where KuzNetzov deposited all material he currently worked on. Some of those
                        - generic [ref=e212]: Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten
                        - generic [ref=e213]: labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few
                        - generic [ref=e214]: of them were marked with red type labels. So specimens belong to the type series were discovered by comparison of their labels with
                        - generic [ref=e215]: the original descriptions. Names of localities mentioned on KuzNEtzov’s labels often differ from modern names and in some cases it
                        - generic [ref=e216]: is difficult to find them on the map. Therefore the list of collecting localities by Kuznetzov is given below with notes on real names
                        - generic [ref=e217]: and coordinates of corresponding places.
                        - generic [ref=e218]: 1. Prov. Sonla, Naniu - According to the map published by Kuznerzov in 2000, this locality is situated between 22° 07° and 22°
                        - generic [ref=e219]: 11° N, 102° 59° and 103° 09° E. Probably this point on the map was identified by KuzNetzov inexactly and actually corres-
                        - generic [ref=e220]: ponds to Ban Nam Nhié situated at 22° 08‘ N, 102° 45‘ E.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:

- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

        - generic [ref=e137]: "Atalanta 41 (3/4): 335-347, Wiirzburg (2010), ISSN 0171-0079 A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by V. I. KUZNETZOv from Vietnam and deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg by SVETLANA V. NEDOSHIVINA received 4.XTI.2009 Abstract: 67 species described by V. KuzNerzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descrip- tions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7-9). Descriptions of 99 of five species are provided and their genitalia are figured. Zusammenfassung: 67 Arten die von V. Kuznetzov aus Vietnam beschrieben wurden, werden mit kurzen Kommentaren zur Ty- pusserie und deren Etikettierung versehen. Die Holotypen werden farbig abgebildet (col. pl. 7-9). Von fünf Arten werden die 99 beschrieben und deren Genitalien abgebildet. Introduction: VLADIMIR IvANovicH KuzNeEtzov (1929-2008) (figs 1-5) is one of the most famous modern Russian lepidopterologists. He was born 28.11.1929 in Kingisepp, Leningrad Region. His father was née Egorov and he was born into the family of a smith. Therefore he was known at school as a smith’s son, in Russian transcription as Kuznetzov (=Kuznetz’s son). Thus, the family name KUZNETZOV is in some sense a pseudonym. During The Second World War Kuznetzov lost his mother and lived in an orphanage until his father came back from the War. After that, VLADIMIR Kuznetzoy finished secondary school in Leningrad and entered the biological faculty of Leningrad State University in 1946. He finished there in 1951 and completed his PhD in 1954. In 1955 Kuz- NETZOV became a staff member at the Zoological Institute of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Leningrad, Russia (ZISP) where he worked for 52 years. He took part in several expeditions and published more than 200 papers devoted to Lepidoptera, especially Tortricidae. Most of his works dealt with the Palaearctic fauna, but some of them were based on material from the Oriental Regi- on. In total, KuzNEtzov described 394 taxa, 295 of them Tortricidae. He died 22. VIII 2008 in St. Petersburg and was cremated at Smolenskoe Cemetery. Twice in his lifetime, in 1986 and 1988, KuzNetzov visited Vietnam as a member of Soviet-Vietnamese zoological expeditions. The first field trip was carried out in spring and all material was collected in the Northern provinces: Son La, Vinh Phuc and Thai Nguyen (earlier Bac Thai). The second trip was in autumn (9.X1.-22.XII.) and during this time KuzNetzov visited the south of the country in the Gia Lai (earlier Gia Lai-Kon Tum) province. A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by KuzNETzov in Vietnam and all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP. As a result of his expeditionary work, Kuznetzov published 13 papers devoted to Tortricidae of Vietnam but only one of them was in English. In these works he listed 225 species, described 67 of them as new, and established 5 new genera. Investigation of the type material is an important part of all taxonomic studies but detailed descriptions of the species, with figured genitalia of both sexes and coloured images of the moths, make the work much easier. Descriptions of Tortricidae from Vietnam published by Kuznetzov in 1988-2003 are quite full and figures of genitalia structures are very good. Unfortunately, he gave no photos of the type specimens and all his descriptions were published in Russian. So the work with KUZNETzov’s papers is very com- plicated without knowledge of the Russian language. In recent years the volume of newly collected material from South-East Asia has really increased; a lot of new species are described recently from this region. At the same time, coloured images are very important for the comparison of new material with the species already described to avoid making synonyms. Since KuZNETzov’s types have never been examined by other workers, almost all of them are placed now in the same genera as in the original description. Very few of them were synonymized and mentioned by other workers at all. The reason is probably the difficulty in interpreting species described by Kuznetzov without images. Another problem is that some species were described by Kuznetzov based on a single specimen, in most cases g, and 99 are unknown. All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by KuZNETZov were arranged taxonomically within the main collection of ZISP. Each speci- men has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality (in English). Most of them have a label with the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text “Ho- lotypus” or “Paratypus” and the name of the species written in ink by KuzNetzov’s hand. KuzNETzov never made genitalia slides and all genitalia preparations are mounted with sugar on the paper plates and put on the species needles under the locality labels. Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, three drawers of Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where KuzNetzov deposited all material he currently worked on. Some of those Tortricidae were determined by him and marked with the species name on a label. Others are undetermined or bear handwritten labels with the name of the genus or different comments (in Russian). All missing types were found in these drawers, but only a few of them were marked with red type labels. So specimens belong to the type series were discovered by comparison of their labels with the original descriptions. Names of localities mentioned on KuzNEtzov’s labels often differ from modern names and in some cases it is difficult to find them on the map. Therefore the list of collecting localities by Kuznetzov is given below with notes on real names and coordinates of corresponding places. 1. Prov. Sonla, Naniu - According to the map published by Kuznerzov in 2000, this locality is situated between 22° 07° and 22° 11° N, 102° 59° and 103° 09° E. Probably this point on the map was identified by KuzNetzov inexactly and actually corres- ponds to Ban Nam Nhié situated at 22° 08‘ N, 102° 45‘ E. 2. Prov. **Paper located:**  
**Nedoshivina, S.V. 2010.** *A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by V.I. Kuznetzov from Vietnam and deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg.* **Atalanta 41(3/4): 335‑347.** ISSN 0171‑0079.

---

## **Abstract** (from the paper)

> “67 species described by V. Kuznetzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descriptions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7‑9). Descriptions of ♀♀ of five species are provided and their genitalia are figured.”

---

## **Deposition information**

The core deposition statement is already in the title: **all type specimens are deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**. The paper provides detailed notes on the actual whereabouts of each type series within the ZISP collections:

### Key passages from the text:

- **Introduction:** “A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by Kuznetzov in Vietnam and **all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **Methods:** “Comments: additional data concerning the type series and number of the type specimens **actually deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **General arrangement:** “All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by Kuznetzov were arranged taxonomically within the **main collection of ZISP**. Each specimen has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality… All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text ‘Holotypus’ or ‘Paratypus’…”  
- **Missing types:** “Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, **three drawers of Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where Kuznetzov deposited all material he currently worked on**… All missing types were found in these drawers…”

### Examples from the catalog (illustrating deposition details):

| Species | Type status | Deposited material (as recorded in the paper) |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| *antecellana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Paratypes | “Although 7 ♂♂, 9 ♀♀ were designated by Kuznetzov as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP are deposited only 5 ♂♂, 7 ♀♀** and one specimen without an abdomen…” |
| *arcuatana* Kuznetzov, 1992 | Paratypes | “Although Kuznetzov designated 11 ♂♂, 58 ♀♀ from Naniu as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP there are 19 ♂♂, 18 ♀♀** collected 9.V.1986 from this locality and marked with Kuznetzov’s handwritten red labels ‘Paratype’.” |
| *assimulatana* Kuznetzov, 1997 | Holotype | “The Holotype was **not found in the main collection of ZISP**. However, in the drawer with Kuznetzov’s material was found a single specimen… **marked with the red printed label ‘HOLOTYPUS’**.” |
| *blanditana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Holotype & paratype | “Holotype, N. Vietnam, prov. Vinhphu, Tamdao, 11.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg. – Paratype: 1 ♂, the same locality, 13.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg.” (both presumed to be in ZISP). |

**In summary:**  
- The **primary repository** for all Kuznetzov’s Vietnamese Tortricidae type material is the **Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**.  
- Most type specimens are housed in the **main collection** under standard red “Holotypus”/“Paratypus” labels.  
- A **supplementary set** of specimens (including some missing types) was found in **Kuznetzov’s personal working drawers** within the same institute.  
- The catalog meticulously documents **discrepancies** between the originally reported type series and the specimens actually present in ZISP.

---

## **Key contents of the paper**

1. **Biographical sketch** of V.I. Kuznetzov (1929‑2008).  
2. **List of collecting localities** in Vietnam with modern coordinates.  
3. **Catalog of 67 Tortricidae species** described by Kuznetzov from Vietnam, each entry providing:
   - Original reference
   - Type series data (holotype/paratype labels, localities, dates)
   - Comments on the specimens actually present in ZISP
   - Distribution notes
   - Taxonomic remarks (updated generic placements, synonyms)
4. **Colour plates** (pl. 7‑9) showing holotypes of all 67 species.  
5. **Taxonomic appendix** with descriptions and genitalia illustrations of previously unknown females of five species:
   - *Statherotis diakonoffi*  
   - *Dicnecidia fumidana*  
   - *Cimeliomorpha nabokovi*  
   - *Neocalyptis sodaliana*  
   - *Homona superbana*  
6. **References** to Kuznetzov’s original works and subsequent revisions.

WebSurfer: **Paper located:**  
**Nedoshivina, S.V. 2010.** *A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by V.I. Kuznetzov from Vietnam and deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg.* **Atalanta 41(3/4): 335‑347.** ISSN 0171‑0079.

---

## **Abstract** (from the paper)

> “67 species described by V. Kuznetzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descriptions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7‑9). Descriptions of ♀♀ of five species are provided and their genitalia are figured.”

---

## **Deposition information**

The core deposition statement is already in the title: **all type specimens are deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**. The paper provides detailed notes on the actual whereabouts of each type series within the ZISP collections:

### Key passages from the text:

- **Introduction:** “A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by Kuznetzov in Vietnam and **all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **Methods:** “Comments: additional data concerning the type series and number of the type specimens **actually deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **General arrangement:** “All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by Kuznetzov were arranged taxonomically within the **main collection of ZISP**. Each specimen has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality… All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text ‘Holotypus’ or ‘Paratypus’…”  
- **Missing types:** “Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, **three drawers of Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where Kuznetzov deposited all material he currently worked on**… All missing types were found in these drawers…”

### Examples from the catalog (illustrating deposition details):

| Species | Type status | Deposited material (as recorded in the paper) |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| *antecellana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Paratypes | “Although 7 ♂♂, 9 ♀♀ were designated by Kuznetzov as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP are deposited only 5 ♂♂, 7 ♀♀** and one specimen without an abdomen…” |
| *arcuatana* Kuznetzov, 1992 | Paratypes | “Although Kuznetzov designated 11 ♂♂, 58 ♀♀ from Naniu as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP there are 19 ♂♂, 18 ♀♀** collected 9.V.1986 from this locality and marked with Kuznetzov’s handwritten red labels ‘Paratype’.” |
| *assimulatana* Kuznetzov, 1997 | Holotype | “The Holotype was **not found in the main collection of ZISP**. However, in the drawer with Kuznetzov’s material was found a single specimen… **marked with the red printed label ‘HOLOTYPUS’**.” |
| *blanditana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Holotype & paratype | “Holotype, N. Vietnam, prov. Vinhphu, Tamdao, 11.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg. – Paratype: 1 ♂, the same locality, 13.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg.” (both presumed to be in ZISP). |

**In summary:**  
- The **primary repository** for all Kuznetzov’s Vietnamese Tortricidae type material is the **Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**.  
- Most type specimens are housed in the **main collection** under standard red “Holotypus”/“Paratypus” labels.  
- A **supplementary set** of specimens (including some missing types) was found in **Kuznetzov’s personal working drawers** within the same institute.  
- The catalog meticulously documents **discrepancies** between the originally reported type series and the specimens actually present in ZISP.

---

1. **Biographical sketch** of V.I. Kuznetzov (1929‑2008).  
2. **List of collecting localities** in Vietnam with modern coordinates.  
3. **Catalog of 67 Tortricidae species** described by Kuznetzov from Vietnam, each entry providing:

   - Comments on the specimens actually present in ZISP
   - Distribution notes
   - Taxonomic remarks (updated generic placements, synonyms)
4. **Colour plates** (pl. 7‑9) showing holotypes of all 67 species.  
5. **Taxonomic appendix** with descriptions and genitalia illustrations of previously unknown females of five species:
   - *Statherotis diakonoffi*  
   - *Dicnecidia fumidana*

WebSurfer: **Paper located:**  
**Nedoshivina, S.V. 2010.** *A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by V.I. Kuznetzov from Vietnam and deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg.* **Atalanta 41(3/4): 335‑347.** ISSN 0171‑0079.

---

## **Abstract** (from the paper)

> “67 species described by V. Kuznetzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descriptions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7‑9). Descriptions of ♀♀ of five species are provided and their genitalia are figured.”

---

## **Deposition information**

The core deposition statement is already in the title: **all type specimens are deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**. The paper provides detailed notes on the actual whereabouts of each type series within the ZISP collections:

### Key passages from the text:

- **Introduction:** “A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by Kuznetzov in Vietnam and **all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **Methods:** “Comments: additional data concerning the type series and number of the type specimens **actually deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **General arrangement:** “All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by Kuznetzov were arranged taxonomically within the **main collection of ZISP**. Each specimen has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality… All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text ‘Holotypus’ or ‘Paratypus’…”  
- **Missing types:** “Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, **three drawers of Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where Kuznetzov deposited all material he currently worked on**… All missing types were found in these drawers…”

### Examples from the catalog (illustrating deposition details):

| Species | Type status | Deposited material (as recorded in the paper) |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| *antecellana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Paratypes | “Although 7 ♂♂, 9 ♀♀ were designated by Kuznetzov as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP are deposited only 5 ♂♂, 7 ♀♀** and one specimen without an abdomen…” |
| *arcuatana* Kuznetzov, 1992 | Paratypes | “Although Kuznetzov designated 11 ♂♂, 58 ♀♀ from Naniu as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP there are 19 ♂♂, 18 ♀♀** collected 9.V.1986 from this locality and marked with Kuznetzov’s handwritten red labels ‘Paratype’.” |
| *assimulatana* Kuznetzov, 1997 | Holotype | “The Holotype was **not found in the main collection of ZISP**. However, in the drawer with Kuznetzov’s material was found a single specimen… **marked with the red printed label ‘HOLOTYPUS’**.” |
| *blanditana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Holotype & paratype | “Holotype, N. Vietnam, prov. Vinhphu, Tamdao, 11.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg. – Paratype: 1 ♂, the same locality, 13.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg.” (both presumed to be in ZISP). |

**In summary:**  
- The **primary repository** for all Kuznetzov’s Vietnamese Tortricidae type material is the **Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**.  
- Most type specimens are housed in the **main collection** under standard red “Holotypus”/“Paratypus” labels.  
- A **supplementary set** of specimens (including some missing types) was found in **Kuznetzov’s personal working drawers** within the same institute.  
- The catalog meticulously documents **discrepancies** between the originally reported type series and the specimens actually present in ZISP.

---

## **Key contents of the paper**

1. **Biographical sketch** of V.I. Kuznetzov (1929‑2008).  
2. **List of collecting localities** in Vietnam with modern coordinates.  
3. **Catalog of 67 Tortricidae species** described by Kuznetzov from Vietnam, each entry providing:
   - Original reference
   - Type series data (holotype/paratype labels, localities, dates)
   - Comments on the specimens actually present in ZISP
   - Distribution notes
   - Taxonomic remarks (updated generic placements, synonyms)
4. **Colour plates** (pl. 7‑9) showing holotypes of all 67 species.  
5. **Taxonomic appendix** with descriptions and genitalia illustrations of previously unknown females of five species:
   - *Statherotis diakonoffi*  
   - *Dicnecidia fumidana*  
   - *Cimeliomorpha nabokovi*  
   - *Neocalyptis sodaliana*  
   - *Homona superbana*  
6. **References** to Kuznetzov’s original works and subsequent revisions.

---

- **Internet Archive page:** [https://archive.org/details/atalanta-41-335-347](https://archive.org/details/atalanta-41-335-347)  
- **Downloadable files** (already retrieved):

The **full text** (including the complete catalog, introduction, appendix, and references) is reproduced above in the snapshot of the text file.

You are the Caller Agent in a hierarchical multi-agent system.
You do not converse directly with other agents. Instead, you invoke them as tools through function calls.

## ABSOLUTE RULE — read this before anything else
Each agent you invoke is completely isolated. It has NO access to conversation history, NO memory of what previous agents did, and can ONLY see the exact text you write into the tool input field — nothing more.
This means: if a previous agent produced output that the current subtask depends on, you MUST copy that output in full, word for word, into the tool input. There are NO exceptions.
The following are strictly FORBIDDEN in any input:
- "[Full changelog text as above]"
- "[as extracted in step 1]"
- "[see previous output]"
- "[full content as above]"
- Any other placeholder, reference, or shorthand that substitutes for actual content

If you write any such phrase, the receiving agent will see only that phrase — not the actual data — and will produce a completely wrong result. Always paste the real content directly.

## Core workflow
Follow the plan strictly, step by step. For each subtask in the plan, invoke the designated agent (with retries only if needed, see Execution rules), then move to the next subtask. After all subtasks have been processed, immediately produce a detailed summary of the entire execution process and output FINISHED. Do not revisit, re-evaluate, or re-execute any subtask that has already been completed.

## Tool call budget
Your total number of allowed tool calls is strictly limited — only slightly more than the number of subtasks in the plan. This budget is intentionally tight: it is enough to execute every subtask once with occasional retries, but not enough to repeat any subtask repeatedly or restart the entire plan. Excessive retries will consume the budget and prevent later subtasks from being executed at all.

## When invoking a tool, you must provide:
- The subtask content from the plan, passed as faithfully and completely as possible. Do not paraphrase, shorten, or omit details from the original subtask description. You may append clarifications, but never replace or reduce the original subtask content.
- All prior output and user-provided information that this subtask depends on, copied verbatim. No summaries. No references. The full actual text.

## Execution rules
- Execute subtasks in order, one at a time. Parallel tool calls are not allowed.
- Each subtask has a maximum of 3 attempts. Retrying is not required — only retry if you judge the result to be a clear failure or clearly insufficient. If the first attempt succeeds, move on immediately.
- If a subtask has been attempted 3 times and still fails, immediately write a detailed summary of the entire execution process so far — including what was attempted, what failed, and why it failed — then output FINISHED. Do not proceed to any remaining subtasks.
- Once all subtasks have been processed (either completed or exhausted their 3 attempts): write a detailed summary of every subtask's execution and result, then output FINISHED. Do this immediately — do not loop back, do not re-check, do not restart.

You never perform tasks yourself. You only control task scheduling, tool invocation, and dependency management.

WebSurfer: **Paper located:**  
**Nedoshivina, S.V. 2010.** *A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by V.I. Kuznetzov from Vietnam and deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg.* **Atalanta 41(3/4): 335‑347.** ISSN 0171‑0079.

---

## **Abstract** (from the paper)

> “67 species described by V. Kuznetzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descriptions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7‑9). Descriptions of ♀♀ of five species are provided and their genitalia are figured.”

---

## **Deposition information**

The core deposition statement is already in the title: **all type specimens are deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**. The paper provides detailed notes on the actual whereabouts of each type series within the ZISP collections:

### Key passages from the text:

- **Introduction:** “A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by Kuznetzov in Vietnam and **all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **Methods:** “Comments: additional data concerning the type series and number of the type specimens **actually deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **General arrangement:** “All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by Kuznetzov were arranged taxonomically within the **main collection of ZISP**. Each specimen has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality… All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text ‘Holotypus’ or ‘Paratypus’…”  
- **Missing types:** “Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, **three drawers of Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where Kuznetzov deposited all material he currently worked on**… All missing types were found in these drawers…”

### Examples from the catalog (illustrating deposition details):

| Species | Type status | Deposited material (as recorded in the paper) |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| *antecellana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Paratypes | “Although 7 ♂♂, 9 ♀♀ were designated by Kuznetzov as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP are deposited only 5 ♂♂, 7 ♀♀** and one specimen without an abdomen…” |
| *arcuatana* Kuznetzov, 1992 | Paratypes | “Although Kuznetzov designated 11 ♂♂, 58 ♀♀ from Naniu as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP there are 19 ♂♂, 18 ♀♀** collected 9.V.1986 from this locality and marked with Kuznetzov’s handwritten red labels ‘Paratype’.” |
| *assimulatana* Kuznetzov, 1997 | Holotype | “The Holotype was **not found in the main collection of ZISP**. However, in the drawer with Kuznetzov’s material was found a single specimen… **marked with the red printed label ‘HOLOTYPUS’**.” |
| *blanditana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Holotype & paratype | “Holotype, N. Vietnam, prov. Vinhphu, Tamdao, 11.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg. – Paratype: 1 ♂, the same locality, 13.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg.” (both presumed to be in ZISP). |

**In summary:**  
- The **primary repository** for all Kuznetzov’s Vietnamese Tortricidae type material is the **Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**.  
- Most type specimens are housed in the **main collection** under standard red “Holotypus”/“Paratypus” labels.  
- A **supplementary set** of specimens (including some missing types) was found in **Kuznetzov’s personal working drawers** within the same institute.  
- The catalog meticulously documents **discrepancies** between the originally reported type series and the specimens actually present in ZISP.

---

## **Key contents of the paper**

1. **Biographical sketch** of V.I. Kuznetzov (1929‑2008).  
2. **List of collecting localities** in Vietnam with modern coordinates.  
3. **Catalog of 67 Tortricidae species** described by Kuznetzov from Vietnam, each entry providing:
   - Original reference
   - Type series data (holotype/paratype labels, localities, dates)
   - Comments on the specimens actually present in ZISP
   - Distribution notes
   - Taxonomic remarks (updated generic placements, synonyms)
4. **Colour plates** (pl. 7‑9) showing holotypes of all 67 species.  
5. **Taxonomic appendix** with descriptions and genitalia illustrations of previously unknown females of five species:
   - *Statherotis diakonoffi*  
   - *Dicnecidia fumidana*  
   - *Cimeliomorpha nabokovi*  
   - *Neocalyptis sodaliana*  
   - *Homona superbana*  
6. **References** to Kuznetzov’s original works and subsequent revisions.

---

## **Abstract** (from the paper)

> “67 species described by V. Kuznetzov from Vietnam are listed with short comments on the type series including descriptions of their labels. Colour images of the holotypes are given (col. pl. 7‑9). Descriptions of ♀♀ of five species are provided and their genitalia are figured.”

## **Deposition information**

The core deposition statement is already in the title: **all type specimens are deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)**. The paper provides detailed notes on the actual whereabouts of each type series within the ZISP collections:

### Key passages from the text:

- **Introduction:** “A huge amount of lepidopterous material was collected by Kuznetzov in Vietnam and **all of it is now deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **Methods:** “Comments: additional data concerning the type series and number of the type specimens **actually deposited in the collection of ZISP**.”  
- **General arrangement:** “All Vietnamese Tortricidae collected by Kuznetzov were arranged taxonomically within the **main collection of ZISP**. Each specimen has a standard white printed label with the name of the locality… All type specimens kept in the main collection have a red label with printed text ‘Holotypus’ or ‘Paratypus’…”  
- **Missing types:** “Surprisingly, types of several species described by Kuznetzov were not found in the main collection. However, **three drawers of Vietnamese Tortricidae were found in the cabinet where Kuznetzov deposited all material he currently worked on**… All missing types were found in these drawers…”

### Examples from the catalog (illustrating deposition details):

| Species | Type status | Deposited material (as recorded in the paper) |
|---------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| *antecellana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Paratypes | “Although 7 ♂♂, 9 ♀♀ were designated by Kuznetzov as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP are deposited only 5 ♂♂, 7 ♀♀** and one specimen without an abdomen…” |
| *arcuatana* Kuznetzov, 1992 | Paratypes | “Although Kuznetzov designated 11 ♂♂, 58 ♀♀ from Naniu as paratypes, **in the collection of ZISP there are 19 ♂♂, 18 ♀♀** collected 9.V.1986 from this locality and marked with Kuznetzov’s handwritten red labels ‘Paratype’.” |
| *assimulatana* Kuznetzov, 1997 | Holotype | “The Holotype was **not found in the main collection of ZISP**. However, in the drawer with Kuznetzov’s material was found a single specimen… **marked with the red printed label ‘HOLOTYPUS’**.” |
| *blanditana* Kuznetzov, 1988 | Holotype & paratype | “Holotype, N. Vietnam, prov. Vinhphu, Tamdao, 11.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg. – Paratype: 1 ♂, the same locality, 13.IV.1986, V. Kuznetzov leg.” (both presumed to be in ZISP). |

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

messages.content:
You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

Using the information gathered: The primary repository for all Kuznetzov's Vietnamese Tortricidae type material is the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP). The paper "A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by V.I. Kuznetzov from Vietnam and deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg" by Nedoshivina (2010) states that all specimens are deposited in ZISP. Most type specimens are housed in the main collection under standard red “Holotypus”/“Paratypus” labels. A supplementary set of specimens (including some missing types) was found in Kuznetzov’s personal working drawers within the same institute. The catalog documents discrepancies between originally reported type series and specimens actually present in ZISP.

Now conduct a second exhaustive search focused on museum collection databases, institutional websites, and biodiversity portals (e.g., GBIF, museum-specific sites) to find independent records confirming the final deposition location of the specified specimens. Use specific museum name "Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)", collection codes, and specimen identifiers (e.g., species names like *antecellana*, *arcuatana*, *assimulatana*, *blanditana*, etc.) from the paper. Retrieve information from multiple relevant sources to perform cross-validation. Specifically search for: "Kuznetzov Vietnamese Tortricidae ZISP", "Zoological Institute St. Petersburg Tortricidae Vietnam", "Nedoshivina 2010 ZISP", "type specimens Kuznetzov Vietnam ZISP". Also search GBIF for records of these species and their institution code ZISP. Find any additional museum records, collection databases, or institutional catalogs that mention the deposition of these specimens. Provide full-breadth retrieval from all located sources, not terminating at the first match.

You are the WebSurfer agent. You retrieve information from the web by navigating and interacting with pages, exactly as a human would.

## Navigation policy
- Unless the user explicitly provides a URL or names a specific website to visit, always start at google.com. Open Google, type your search query, read the results, and follow links by clicking — do not jump directly to any URL, and do not construct or guess URLs from memory or training data.

## Page size management (critical)
Loading large, unfiltered pages makes it hard to locate relevant information and risks exceeding LLM context length limits. Before loading any page, actively try to reduce its size:
- Use the site's search box with specific keywords rather than browsing index pages.
- Apply any available filters: date range, category, author, language, file type, etc.
- Prefer paginated or scoped views over full listing pages.

## Tool selection
- Prefer specialized tools (ArXiv, Wikipedia, YouTube, direct download, etc.) when they directly match the task. Use browser automation only when no dedicated tool fits.
- Only Google Search is permitted as a search engine.
- For academic paper searches, prefer Google Scholar, arXiv, and DBLP.

## Output
- Produce well-structured, detailed output as required. Extract only what is relevant to the task.
- If you use browser tools to save any content, the browser will store it under the directory: [<PROJECT_ROOT>/tmp/browser_wp]. This is enforced by the browser itself — you only need to report the file path in your output when needed.

Work carefully, efficiently, and stay within your assigned retrieval scope.

Using the information gathered: The primary repository for all Kuznetzov's Vietnamese Tortricidae type material is the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP). The paper "A catalogue of type specimens of the Tortricidae described by V.I. Kuznetzov from Vietnam and deposited in the Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg" by Nedoshivina (2010) states that all specimens are deposited in ZISP. Most type specimens are housed in the main collection under standard red “Holotypus”/“Paratypus” labels. A supplementary set of specimens (including some missing types) was found in Kuznetzov’s personal working drawers within the same institute. The catalog documents discrepancies between originally reported type series and specimens actually present in ZISP.

Now conduct a second exhaustive search focused on museum collection databases, institutional websites, and biodiversity portals (e.g., GBIF, museum-specific sites) to find independent records confirming the final deposition location of the specified specimens. Use specific museum name "Zoological Institute, St. Petersburg (ZISP)", collection codes, and specimen identifiers (e.g., species names like *antecellana*, *arcuatana*, *assimulatana*, *blanditana*, etc.) from the paper. Retrieve information from multiple relevant sources to perform cross-validation. Specifically search for: "Kuznetzov Vietnamese Tortricidae ZISP", "Zoological Institute St. Petersburg Tortricidae Vietnam", "Nedoshivina 2010 ZISP", "type specimens Kuznetzov Vietnam ZISP". Also search GBIF for records of these species and their institution code ZISP. Find any additional museum records, collection databases, or institutional catalogs that mention the deposition of these specimens. Provide full-breadth retrieval from all located sources, not terminating at the first match.
